hero.eyebrow: a taste engine for the web
hero.title: Describe a site. Get its taste.
hero.sub: One sentence in. A design recipe drawn from ten thousand real references out, then a page composed from it, section by section.

how_it_works.title: Three steps, each one inspectable
steps: Your sentence becomes two queries: what the site is for, and how it should feel.
The feeling is routed through 39 aesthetic families to a palette, a type pairing, a scale and imagery from that family's folders.
Sections are built inside a frame the recipe defines, then checked: contrast, fonts, no scripts, no stray colours.

showcase.title: Every family keeps its own folders
showcase.sub: Website captures, UI kits, 3D renders, illustration, type specimens and palettes, grouped by CLIP. The studio pulls from the routed family's folders for each section.

faq.title: Questions
items: Where do the images come from?
A research corpus of public design references, clustered into 39 aesthetic families. They are shown only to signed-in testers and credited as references.
Is any of this written by AI?
Not right now. Sections are composed from the lab's design decisions and a copy kit; a language model can fill the copy later without changing the design.
What keeps it from looking generic?
The recipe decides palette, type, scale, alignment and imagery from real references, and guardrails repair anything that fails contrast or the vibe's own cues.
